weeks.label: Week 1

motor.text: Tummy time on your chest — 1–2 min skin-to-skin, 2–3× daily
Gentle limb cycling — move legs slowly like a bicycle, 10 reps

social.text: Hold baby within 20–30 cm of your face and make gentle eye contact
Talk softly to baby during every feed and nappy change

cognitive.text: Play a soft lullaby or Quranic recitation — 5–10 min
Show a high-contrast black-and-white card for 1 min

watch: Baby startles at loud sounds (Moro reflex)
Baby turns head toward a sound source
Baby's gaze follows your face briefly

weeks.label: Weeks 2–3

motor.text: Tummy time on a firm surface — 3–5 min, 3× daily
Gentle neck stretches — support head and tilt slowly side to side

social.text: Mirror baby's expressions — stick out your tongue and wait for imitation
Narrate your day aloud while caring for baby

cognitive.text: Slowly move a high-contrast toy across baby's field of vision — tracking practice
Introduce a different texture to baby's palm (soft cloth, smooth rubber)

watch: First social smile (reflex smile from gas is earlier — social smile is directed at you)
Baby tracks a moving object 45–90 degrees
Baby lifts chin briefly during tummy time

weeks.label: Week 4

motor.text: Tummy time 5–10 min, 3–4× daily — build up gradually
Supported sitting briefly in your lap — let baby feel upright weight

social.text: Respond to every coo with a coo back — the first 'conversation'
Kangaroo care 1 hour — skin-to-skin regulates temperature and heart rate

cognitive.text: Hang a simple mobile above baby — 30–40 cm away, high contrast
Read a board book aloud — voice rhythm matters more than meaning

watch: Baby holds eye contact for 5–10 seconds
Baby lifts head 45° during tummy time
Baby's hands open and close less reflexively

weeks.label: Weeks 5–6

motor.text: Tummy time target: 15–20 min total spread across the day
Baby sit-ups: hold baby's hands and gently pull to sitting (head may lag — support it)

social.text: Smile and wait — let baby initiate a smile back (social reciprocity)
Sing the same 2–3 songs every day — repetition builds expectation and security

cognitive.text: Track a slow-moving rattle — horizontal and then vertical arcs
Introduce cause-and-effect: squeeze a squeaky toy so baby hears the result

watch: Consistent social smiling when you make eye contact
Baby vocalises in response to your voice (cooing)
Head lags are reduced — baby tries to hold head up

weeks.label: Weeks 7–8

motor.text: Offer a finger to grasp during alert time — strengthens palmar grasp
Tummy time on a rolled towel under chest — elevates head and chest for easier lift

social.text: Gentle tickle around ribs — first giggles often appear this week
Peek-a-boo with a soft cloth — object permanence seeds begin

cognitive.text: Show baby their reflection in a baby-safe mirror — fascination is normal
Vary your voice tone and speed when speaking — baby learns prosody

watch: First laugh or giggle
Baby bats at a hanging toy intentionally
Head control: baby holds head steady at 90° for several seconds

weeks.label: Weeks 9–10

motor.text: Batting gym: hang toys at chest height so baby can swat with both arms
Supported tummy time — mini push-ups: chest lifts off surface using arms

social.text: Hold baby facing outward — let them watch household activity for 10 min
Name emotions as they happen: 'You're happy!' 'That scared you — it's okay'

cognitive.text: Put a soft rattle in baby's hand and let them shake it — cause and effect
Read with your finger tracing under text — eye-tracking practice

watch: Baby brings hands together at midline
Baby reaches for objects intentionally (not just reflex grasp)
Baby shows clear preference for familiar voices and faces

weeks.label: Weeks 11–12

motor.text: Encourage side-lying: roll baby gently to their side, see if they roll to back
Supported standing: hold baby under armpits and let feet push on a firm surface

social.text: Introduce baby to 1 new person or face (outside family) — social widening
Play copycat: make a mouth shape, wait, see if baby copies

cognitive.text: Let baby feel 3 different textures today: smooth, rough, soft
Name everything you hand to baby — label the world constantly

watch: Baby rolls from back to side (full rolls come by 4–5 months)
Drooling increases — teething prep, not actual teeth yet
Baby quiets to a familiar song or voice

weeks.label: Months 4–5

motor.text: Practice supported sitting in a pillow ring or on your lap — 5–10 min
Encourage rolling by placing toys just out of reach on each side
Standing pressure: hold baby standing, let them bounce on your lap

social.text: Serve and return conversation: wait for baby's vocalisation, respond, wait again
Introduce simple sign language: 'milk', 'more', 'all done'

cognitive.text: Bring baby to the kitchen during cooking — narrate smells, sounds, actions
Stack 2 blocks in front of baby and knock them down — show cause and effect

watch: Baby rolls front-to-back and back-to-front
Baby explores objects by mouthing them
Babbling begins (ba, ma, da sounds)

weeks.label: Month 6

motor.text: Practice tripod sitting (baby uses both hands in front for balance)
Introduce spoon feeding or baby-led weaning — whichever you have chosen

social.text: Let baby play in front of a large mirror — recognising self begins
Narrate emotions visibly: exaggerated surprise, joy, concern — baby reads your face

cognitive.text: Introduce object permanence: hide a toy under a cloth while baby watches
Read 3 different board books today — variety builds vocabulary

watch: Sits unsupported briefly (6 months milestone)
Transfers objects from hand to hand
Stranger anxiety may begin — normal and healthy

weeks.label: Months 7–8

motor.text: Crawling prep: rocking on all-fours, then shift weight forward and back
Pincer practice: offer small puffs or soft bits for them to pick up with 2 fingers

social.text: Play turn-taking games: roll a ball back and forth
Point to objects and name them — joint attention builds vocabulary

cognitive.text: Let baby bang two objects together — rhythm and cause-and-effect
Peek-a-boo with full hide: disappear behind a door and reappear — object permanence

watch: Army crawl or full hands-and-knees crawl
Pulls to standing using furniture
Says 'mama' or 'dada' without specific meaning

weeks.label: Month 9

motor.text: Cruising practice: walk along the sofa edge holding baby's hand as they step
Stair climbing: supervised crawl up 2–3 steps and back down

social.text: Read a book with pointing: 'Where is the dog?' — wait for baby to point or look
Celebrate every attempt at a new word or sound effusively

cognitive.text: Simple shape sorting — even if baby just mouths the shapes, that is learning
Introduce nesting cups — in/out, bigger/smaller concepts begin

watch: Waves bye-bye on request
Points to indicate interest (proto-declarative pointing)
Uses 1–2 words with consistent meaning

weeks.label: Months 10–11

motor.text: Push-toy walking: let baby push a stable trolley or laundry basket across the room
Throwing practice: sit across from baby and roll a ball, encourage them to throw back

social.text: Pretend play: feed a doll, drive a toy car — baby starts imitating domestic acts
Follow the child's lead — let them choose the activity for 10 minutes

cognitive.text: Simple puzzles: 2–3 piece knob puzzles
Name body parts on a doll or on baby themselves: 'Where is your nose?'

watch: Takes first independent steps (typically 9–12 months)
Says 2–3 words with meaning
Follows simple 1-step instructions ('give me the ball')

weeks.label: Month 12

motor.text: Walking practice: encourage walking to you across the room
Climbing: supervised climbing onto a low sofa cushion placed on the floor

social.text: Playdate with another child — parallel play (not interactive yet) is normal and healthy
Celebrate their first birthday with presence, not presents — they want you, not stuff

cognitive.text: Let baby 'help' with tasks: handing you things, pressing the elevator button
Ask 'where is ___?' for 5 different familiar objects — vocabulary comprehension check

watch: 10+ words (some babies have more, some fewer — comprehension matters more than output at 12m)
Points and looks at you to share interest (joint attention)
Plays pretend (feeds a doll, holds phone to ear)
